issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for an arbitrary j-th eigenpair, which may be multiple or defective. Dividing the identity $(\lambda_h-\lambda)(u_h,v_h)$ by $|(u_h,v_h)|$ needs $|(u,u^*)|$ to be bounded away from zero. For a defective eigenvalue, primal and adjoint eigenvectors are orthogonal, so $(u,u^*)=0$. For a multiple semisimple eigenvalue, independently normalized j-th primal and adjoint eigenvectors need not be biorthogonal and can also give $(u,u^*)=0$. In either case the bound fails. The appeal to an external lemma does not supply these missing hypotheses. Moreover, for defective eigenvalues the error is known to behave like $h^{2s/\alpha}$, so a quadratic bound cannot hold there.

failure_location.quote: we deduce that $|(\mathbf{u}_{h},\mathbf{v}_{h})|$ has a positive lower bound uniformly with respect to $h$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a simple, or semisimple non-defective, eigenvalue with biorthogonally normalized primal and adjoint eigenfunctions, prove the lower bound under that assumption, and restrict Theorem th3-8 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Estimate (s2.78) is unsupported for multiple or defective eigenvalues. The eigenvalue estimate (s2.85) loses its justification for multiple eigenvalues, and the eigenvalue reliability bound (s3.33) loses it outside the simple, non-defective case.
issues.title: Uniform lower bound for |(u_h, v_h)| asserted without the hypotheses that make it true
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a hypothesis and a short argument. The defective case advertised for the eigenvalue estimator is lost, but comparable results survive for non-defective eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: Bound (s3.12) involves the l1 sums $\sum_\tau(\eta_{R_\tau}+\eta_{F_\tau}+\eta_{J_\tau})$ and $\sum_\tau\|div\,u_h\|_{0,\tau}$. These sums can exceed $\eta_h=(\sum_\tau\eta_\tau^2)^{1/2}$ by a factor of up to $\sqrt{N}$. Substituting (s3.12) into (s3.8) therefore does not give (s3.22), which is stated with $\eta_h$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (s3.12)-(s3.13) in l2 form, which (s3.15) and Cauchy-Schwarz on the jump and divergence terms already yield, and then substitute.
issues.overall_effect: The reliability estimate (s3.22)-(s3.23) is not delivered by the cited lemma as stated.
issues.title: Reliability bound for the l2 estimator derived from a lemma stated with l1 sums
issues.why_classification: This is a local restatement that the proof already supports. The bound and rate are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: In (s3.30) the face term $\int_F[\![(u_h-u)\otimes\beta]\!]\cdot\bar\Theta$ involves the jump of the discontinuous $u_h$. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds it by $h_F^{1/2}\|[\![u_h]\!]\|_{0,F}\|R\|_{0,F}$. This is a jump contribution, not controlled by $\|\nabla(u-u_h)\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}$, the pressure error or the data terms. The right-hand side of (s3.25) contains none of these jump terms, so it does not follow.

failure_location.quote: and by (\ref{s3.24}) and Proposition 3.37 in \cite{Verfurth2013}, we get (\ref{s3.25}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term $h_F^{1/2}\cdot h_F^{-1/2}\|[\![u_h]\!]\|_{0,F}$ (part of the DG norm) to the right-hand sides of (s3.25) and (s3.28).
issues.overall_effect: The stated local bound (s3.25), and likewise (s3.28), is unsupported. Theorem th3-6 survives because its right-hand side contains $\|u-u_h\|_h$, which includes the jumps.
issues.title: Local efficiency bound for eta_F omits the contribution of the convective jump
issues.why_classification: Adding one local term repairs it. The global efficiency result is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding (s2.78) through (s3.22)-(s3.23) introduces the terms $\|\lambda_hu_h-\lambda u\|_0^2$ and $\|\lambda_h^*u_h^*-\lambda^*u^*\|_0^2$. The term $\lambda(u-u_h,u^*-u_h^*)$ needs an L2 control that the estimators do not provide. None of these terms appears in (s3.33), and no argument removes them.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the omitted terms to (s3.33), and argue that they are of higher order using the a priori L2 estimates (s2.81) and (s2.83) in the non-defective case.
issues.overall_effect: Inequality (s3.33) as stated is not established. Only a version that includes these extra error terms is proved.
issues.title: Eigenvalue bound drops terms that its own proof produces
issues.why_classification: The statement is corrected locally by adding terms. The method and rates are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as well as the reliability of the estimator for approximate eigenvalues

issues.failure_explanation: The extra terms in (s3.33) are interpolation errors of the unknown exact eigenpairs, not data oscillations. They scale like $h^{2r}h^{2(s-r)}=h^{2s}$, the same order as $\eta_h^2$ and as the eigenvalue error $h^{2s}$, so they are not of higher order. Dropping them gives a third inequality, $|\lambda_i-\lambda_{i,h}|\lesssim\sum(\eta^2+\eta^{*2})$, that is unproved. The advertised computable reliability for eigenvalues is therefore not established.

failure_location.quote: and up to the oscillation terms, we can obtain the following corollary.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the face terms $h_F^{1/2}\|\{\nabla(u-u_h)\}\|_F$ in the eigenvalue identity by computable quantities, for example via a lifting or enriching-operator argument with local efficiency, giving $|\lambda-\lambda_h|\lesssim\eta^2+\eta^{*2}$ plus true higher-order terms.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract's claim of reliability of the eigenvalue estimator is not supported by the paper. Only a bound involving uncomputable terms of the same order is shown.
issues.title: Same-order interpolation errors of the exact eigenfunctions discarded as 'oscillation terms'
issues.why_classification: Restoring the computable eigenvalue bound needs a contained new argument; the result is otherwise lost. No global restructuring is required.
